relevance_note: The paper gives individual-level detail for one in-scope person, patient 3, who carries a biallelic ALDH5A1 variant ('ALDH5A1:c.803G>A;p.Gly268Glu Biallelic') in a cohort of patients with congenital ataxia.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules; no script was used, the single table row and the checklist were transcribed by hand. In-scope people: the Table lists 29 of the 30 enrolled patients and only row 3 has an ALDH5A1 variant, so only patient 3 gets rows; the other cohort members (including the sibling pairs 16/17 and 22/23/24 and the relatives mentioned in the Discussion) have no ALDH5A1 variant and no stated SSADH diagnosis and are out of scope, counted in cohort_size_as_stated = 30. Label: the Table's 'Patients' column holds bare numbers and the paper never names this person in the text, while its most-used label form elsewhere is 'patient N' (e.g. 'patient 27'), so the label used here is 'patient 3'. The Table is unnumbered ('presented in the Table'). No ' / ' stacked cells occur in the Table; rows 16/17 and 22/23/24 list siblings in one row but are out of scope. No per-patient reference/source column exists, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported'. Zygosity: the row prints 'Biallelic' for this single variant and the Discussion states 'Pathogenic homozygous variants were found in 3 genes: ALDH5A1, EXOSC3, and SNX14.'; recorded as homozygous. variant_type_as_stated left 'not reported' because the authors never name a variant class for this variant (not derived from the HGVS string). is_proband and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper never calls this person a proband/index case and never states that any of its patients were reported earlier, so no verbatim span exists. Checklist 'ataxia' marked observed from the group statement naming all thirty enrolled patients ('diagnosed with congenital ataxia'); the cohort's inclusion criteria were not used as evidence. 'developmental delay' was not mapped onto the checklist item 'gross or fine motor deficits' (the paper does not call it motor delay for this person). Inconsistencies found in the paper: the Table jumps from patient 13 to 15 (no row 14, 29 of 30 patients shown); row 30 has a shifted cell (a CACNA1A variant string sits in the Brain structure on MRI column); Figure 2C reports 'a pathogenic homozygous mutation in the ALDH5A1 gene' without naming the patient, so it was not used as evidence about patient 3; the Discussion's SSADH deficiency description is about the ALDH5A1 gene in general, not about this person, so it was not recorded as this person's diagnosis.
